doc.title: Mona Hinton interviewed by Milt Fillius and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: The Mona Hinton Fund and church tutoring
summary: The church's Saturday tutoring program for children, with professionals donating time.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well we’ll come back to that in a minute. I want to switch you to another phase of your life that I know is important to you, and that’s the work that you do with your church and the Mona Hinton Fund and the work that’s done with that. And the thing that amazes me about that is that you have time to do it.
Could you tell us what the work is?

Well I’ll tell you that we raised this money, and on Saturdays we have, at our church, the children from first grade on up to college, up through high school, can come and they introduce them to various, well not occupations, just various well they are occupations I guess but that’s not the word I wanted to use. But anyway, they are tutored as I say from first grade through the eighth grade, I mean through the high school, and they have a lot of young black young men who are in various professions such as computers and attorneys, I mean, and various professions. And what they do is come and they donate their time to working with these youngsters. And it’s, they’re just doing a magnificent job, magnificent job, of helping these youngsters, I mean help to try to further theirselves,
I mean improve their, you know, improve their way of wanting to live, their methods and their lifestyles. And basically that’s what they’re doing.
Exactly. As I say, it’s doing an excellent job.
But that operation has your name on it.
